prompt_text: Where should I stay in Branson Missouri, an Airbnb or a hotel, and which specific places are best?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer
- If you want convenience, fixed schedules (shows, restaurants), on‑site amenities and easy parking: pick a hotel on or near the 76 Strip or Branson Landing.
- If you want more space, a kitchen, lake or woods privacy, or you’re traveling with a group/family: pick an Airbnb/cabin/condo (often better value per person).

Which to choose (quick pros & cons)
- Hotel
  - Pros: daily housekeeping, front desk, on‑site restaurants/pools/spa, predictable check‑in, close to shows.
  - Cons: smaller rooms, extra fees (resort/parking), less privacy, can be pricey for families.
- Airbnb / cabin / condo
  - Pros: whole‑house living room and kitchen, more bedrooms, outdoor space/hot tub, lake or forest settings, good for groups.
  - Cons: variable quality, sometimes strict check‑in rules, cleaning/cancellation policies differ, fewer on‑site services.

Where to stay by travel style (specific recommendations and areas)
- Want luxury / lakefront relaxation
  - Chateau on the Lake Resort Spa & Convention Center (Table Rock Lake) — upscale lake views, spa, good for adults/couples.
  - Big Cedar Lodge area (Ridgedale/Top of the Rock / Big Cedar properties) — rustic luxury, lots of outdoor activities (a short drive from the Strip).
- Want convenience to shows, shopping, nightlife (best for first-time Branson visitors)
  - Hotels on/near 76 Country Boulevard (the “Strip”): look at Radisson Hotel Branson, Hilton Branson Convention Center (or comparable large hotels on the Strip), Stone Castle Hotel — all put you near theaters and restaurants.
  - Branson Landing (downtown on Lake Taneycomo): convenient for shopping, restaurants, some lakefront views — condos/hotels here keep you walkable to the Landing.
- Family or group stays where cost per person matters
  - Welk Resort Branson (condo units, resort pools/activities).
  - Still Waters Resort or other condo resorts on Table Rock Lake / Lake Taneycomo — condos with multiple bedrooms and kitchens.
  - Large Airbnbs / cabins near Silver Dollar City (great if that’s your main reason to visit).
- Outdoors / boating / fishing
  - Table Rock Lake & Indian Point area — private cabins and condos with docks, great for fishing/boats.
  - Branson West / near Silver Dollar City if you want quick access to the theme park and Ozark outdoor trails.
- Budget options
  - Chain motels and mid‑range hotels (Best Western, Comfort Inn, Baymont) on US‑65 and side streets — simple, cheaper, usually driveable to attractions.

Practical tips for choosing a specific place
- If you plan to center your trip on shows and dinner theaters, stay on/near the 76 Strip or Branson Landing to minimize driving and maximize walkability.
- If you’ll boat, fish, or want a peaceful getaway, search for lakefront cabins/condos on Table Rock Lake or Lake Taneycomo.
- For groups, a whole‑house Airbnb or a condo with multiple bedrooms + kitchen almost always saves money over hotel rooms.
- Check recent guest reviews (last 3–6 months) for cleanliness and host responsiveness.
- Filter Airbnbs for “Entire place,” “hot tub” or “dock” if important; prefer Superhosts with lots of 5‑star reviews.
- Book early for summer and fall festival/weekend dates — rates and availability change quickly.

Price ranges (ballpark)
- Budget hotels: ~$70–130/night (off/shoulder season cheaper).
- Mid‑range hotels/resorts: ~$120–250/night.
- Luxury lakefront / Big Cedar / Chateau: $250+ (can be much more in peak season).
- Cabins/Airbnbs: $120–400+/night depending on size, lake access, and season.

If you want a tailored shortlist
Tell me: travel dates, number of people (adults/kids), must‑have features (kitchen, hot tub, lake access, pet friendly), and budget per night — I’ll pick 4–6 specific hotels and Airbnb/cabin options with pros/cons and distance to the Strip and Silver Dollar City.
